description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs: Three locations cast usize as u32 without overflow check.

1. Line 1643: modulus_byte_len.saturating_mul(8) as u32 — byte length of RSA modulus is bounded in practice (~8 KiB max enforced elsewhere), but the cast is visibly unchecked. A comment bounding the range or u32::try_from would be clearer and avoids surprising any future reader.

2. Lines 1728, 1733, 1738: (n as u32).saturating_add(1) where n = chain.len(). n is a usize counting certs in the chain. On a 64-bit target a chain with >4 billion certs would truncate n before the saturating_add, producing a wrong counter value. Fix: u32::try_from(n).unwrap_or(u32::MAX) or keep counters as usize throughout (they only need to count to n+1).

Clippy pedantic fires: 'casting usize to u32 may truncate the value on targets with 64-bit wide pointers'
title: usize-to-u32 cast in rsa_public_key_bits and policy counters can truncate
